newsitem.title: USA: Olympics guard Jewell says he will sue press.
newsitem.headline: Olympics guard Jewell says he will sue press.

text.p: Security guard Richard Jewell, named by FBI sources in press reports as a suspect in the Olympics park bombing, says in a television interview to be shown on Sunday that he and his lawyers plan to sue everyone who has libelled him -- even if it takes years.
Telling CBS "60 Minutes" that the press descended on him like "piranha," an angry Jewell added, "and they haven't even finished picking the bone yet."

Ever since a local newspaper said Jewell was considered a suspect in the July 27 bombing in which two people died and 110 were injured, he has been living like a recluse, unable to work or travel freely.
The FBI refuses to state publicly what conclusions it has reached about him, while his lawyers claim he is totally innocent of any involvement.

"People will be 90 years old that were at the Olympic Games and go: 'Do you remember when the bomb went off? That Jewell fellow they accused of that?' It will never end," Jewell said, adding that the accusation has ended his chance of a career in law enforcement.

"Would you want a fellow in your employ that had as much press, both negative and positive, that I have had? If I arrest somebody and something goes wrong, which happens every day, am I going to have 50 press show up? And just for that reason alone, I don't think (getting another job in law enforcement) is going to happen."

He added: "Myself and my attorneys are looking at everyone and anyone who has said libellous things (about me). It might be a year, it might be six years, but everybody ... will be hearing from one of my attorneys."
